text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, maker of luxury Mercedes cars, said on Thursday it was recalling 176,000 vehicles worldwide due to problems with their braking systems.
In affected vehicles the brakes could overreact to a slight push on the brake pedal. Cars needed to be brought to garages for new components to be installed, a company spokesman said.
The brake system problem affects a series of Mercedes models, and was first noticed in the S-class luxury saloon, and the SL cabriolet at the end of 1996.
Since March, the E-class executive range and since June the C-class saloon and CLK cabriolet have also been diagnosed with the defect.
The spokesman said that new brake sensors were now being built into cars under production.

The Mercedes braking system was designed to recognise emergency situations and engage at full power. Accident research has shown that drivers often do not step on the brakes hard enough to avoid accidents, the spokesman explained.
Of the total, some 88,000 vehicles are affected in Germany and can be repaired for free, he said.
